title: Security Enablement Kit v2 — Working Outline + Owners (GTM package)
content:
Last updated: 2026-01-15 (Naomi)
Status: drafting / gap inventory

Purpose
- Create a single, consistent “Enterprise Security Enablement Kit” package for Sales + SEs + CS to use in late-stage security review + procurement.
- Reduce ad hoc answers and “version drift” across: Confluence vs Drive PDFs vs email attachments vs questionnaire copy/paste.
- Make “Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private” boundaries explicit everywhere.

Non-goals / guardrails (repeat everywhere)
- No new security feature commitments.
- Avoid absolute language (“always/never”, exact incident notification timelines unless contractually agreed).
- Anything restricted (SOC 2 report, pen test report) must follow evidence sharing SOP (NDA + tracking).

Primary field asks (from AEs/SEs)
- “Give me one link to the latest kit” (see Slack:sales/1708535099)
- Pre-approved incident notification wording + what counts as a security incident/breach (see Slack:sales/1708451122)
- Clear data retention + deletion statement (esp. for renewal reviews)
- Clear data residency posture by deployment mode (EMEA blocker theme)
- Audit log scope: what’s logged today vs roadmap; export/streaming options; sample events

Deliverables (v2 refresh)
1) Security FAQ v2 (customer-facing, field shareable PDF + canonical Confluence)
2) Compliance & Security One-Pagers pack (PDF slides + canonical Confluence pages)
3) Standard RFP response library (canonical Confluence + “question bank” sheet)
4) Internal evidence pointer index (internal-only) (ENG-23344)

Packaging / where things live (proposed)
- Canonical source of truth: Confluence pages (versioned + last reviewed date)
- Field package: Drive PDFs (controlled sharing; easy attachments)
- “Single link”: Confluence landing page that points to the latest Drive folder + notes on access restrictions
- CRM linking: HubSpot snippets/links to the Confluence landing page (Isabelle)

Folder structure (Drive)
- shared_drives/go-to-market/security-enablement-kit-v2/
  - 00_README_(how_to_share)_and_access_controls
  - 01_Security_FAQ/
    - Security_FAQ_v2_(PDF)
  - 02_One_Pagers/
    - One_Pagers_Pack_v2_(PDF)
    - Individual_exports/
  - 03_RFP_Library/
    - Link_to_Confluence_canonical
    - Question_Bank_(sheet)
  - 04_Restricted_Evidence_(DO_NOT_SHARE)
    - (empty; link to internal Confluence SOP instead)

Kit v2 table of contents (field-facing)
A. Quick cover note (1 page)
- What this package is / when to use
- Which deployment modes are covered
- How to request evidence / security review escalation path
Owner: Naomi + Soojin

B. Enterprise Security FAQ v2 (main doc)
- Audience: security reviewers + procurement + IT admins
- Includes: deployment modes shared responsibility; encryption; auth/SSO/RBAC; audit logs; retention/residency; vuln mgmt; incident response
Owner: Naomi (coordination) / reviewers Marcus + Olga + Markus Klein

C. One-pagers (each should stand alone in email)
Required list (v2):
1) Compliance posture / SOC 2 summary
- Goal: explain SOC 2 Type II availability + how to request report under NDA
Owner: Olga Petrov (approver), Daniel Carter (evidence flow)
Notes: keep it high-level; do NOT paste report content into PDF.

2) Encryption & key management
- In transit + at rest; customer options (KMS/HSM integrations esp. Private)
Owner: Marcus Lin (approver) + Colin O’Donnell (Private boundary)
Outdated note: current v1 one-pager implies “customer-managed keys” universally; needs mode-specific phrasing.

3) SSO / SAML / SCIM + RBAC model
- What’s supported; enterprise setup pattern; auditability
Owner: Ethan Park + Kaitlyn Nguyen (SMEs); Naomi (final language)
Open question: SCIM availability/limitations by plan and by deployment mode; avoid over-committing.

4) Audit logging overview
- What events exist today; retention; export/forwarding; Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private differences
Owner: Kevin Osei (SME) + Marcus Lin (approval)
Open question: “export” wording (pull vs push; SIEM integration patterns). Keep to what’s GA.

5) Data residency (regions + controls) one-pager
- Region availability; where request processing occurs; where logs/telemetry go; Dedicated/Private differences
Owner: Kira Thompson + Vivek Kulkarni (review) + Lukas Meyer (EMEA field sanity)
Open question: exact language for “processing region” vs “storage region” vs “support access”.

6) Data retention controls one-pager
- Defaults; configurable retention where available; deletion request process; audit log retention considerations
Owner: Kevin Osei + Olga Petrov
Outdated note: v1 doc says “30 days by default” in multiple places—verify current defaults before publishing.

7) Incident response & notification one-pager
- Our process; how we communicate; contract-dependent timelines; status page reference
Owner: Marcus Lin + Olga Petrov + Legal reviewer (Michael Grant)
Notes: align to approved wording from Slack:sales/1708451122; remove “72 hours” default claim unless contract.

8) Secure SDLC summary (optional but strongly recommended)
- Code review; scanning; vuln remediation; release process
Owner: Marcus Lin (final) + Docs support (Elliot Price)

D. Standard RFP Response Library
- Canonical answers + variants by deployment mode
- Evidence pointers + “who to ask” routing (Security/GRC/Legal)
Owner: Naomi + Markus Klein + Olga
Must include:
- “How to answer” guardrails
- “If customer asks for X evidence” do Y process
- Approved copy blocks for:
  - SOC 2 availability + report sharing
  - pen test summary sharing process
  - subprocessors list location + update cadence
  - DPA / legal routing

E. Internal-only content (do NOT ship to customers)
- Evidence pointer index (ENG-23344)
- SOP: customer security review process (restricted Confluence)
Owner: Daniel Carter + Olga

Standard page template (for one-pagers)
- Title
- What it is (2–3 bullets)
- What Redwood provides
- What customer controls (esp. Dedicated/Private)
- Deployment mode differences table (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)
- FAQ / common reviewer questions
- Evidence / how to request (if applicable)
- Footer: owner + last reviewed + doc version
Owner: Soojin (format), Elliot (publishing hygiene)

Outdated / inconsistent content to fix (known)
- Incident notification: v1 materials have conflicting timing language; Sales has been copy/pasting from old email templates.
- Audit logging: v1 implies “all API requests are logged with full prompts/responses” (not accurate; needs careful wording about what is and isn’t included).
- Retention: multiple defaults floating around; need one approved statement + where configurable.
- Data residency: confusion between “region where inference runs” and “where operational telemetry/logs may be processed.”
- Private deployment boundary: current slides blur responsibilities (customer-managed infra vs Redwood-managed control plane components). Must be explicit.
- SSO/SCIM: unclear if SCIM is supported for all enterprise plans; also unclear what’s available in Private.
- Subprocessors: ensure we have one authoritative place and don’t embed a static list into PDFs.

Open questions / decisions needed
1) Evidence sharing: what do we include as “safe to share without NDA”? (SOC 2 cover letter? bridge letter? pen test attestation?)
- Owner: Olga + Daniel
- Output: a simple table: artifact / NDA required / who sends / turnaround SLA.

2) Data retention: confirm defaults per product surface (API logs, console audit logs, telemetry).
- Owner: Kevin + Nikhil (Hosted) + Lauren (Dedicated) + Vivek (Private)
- Output: one approved paragraph + table by data type.

3) Audit log scope: define the minimum list of event categories we can claim today.
- Owner: Kevin + Marcus
- Output: categories list + examples (non-sensitive).

4) Data residency: what’s our exact public position on EU processing and support access?
- Owner: Olga + Lukas + Legal
- Output: mode-specific language; avoid “guarantees” unless contractual.

5) Private deployment: confirm shared responsibility model diagram language.
- Owner: Colin + Vivek + Marcus
- Output: a consistent diagram + 5–7 bullet boundary summary.

Review + approval workflow (draft)
- Draft in Drive (tracked edits)
- Reviewers:
  - Security Eng: Marcus Lin
  - GRC/Compliance: Olga Petrov
  - Product/Mode SMEs: Nikhil (Hosted), Lauren (Dedicated), Vivek (Private)
  - Solutions Eng: Markus Klein (field usability + objection handling)
  - Legal (customer-facing claims): Michael Grant or Sofia Mendes (as needed)
- Publish to Confluence as canonical
- Export PDFs to Drive (field package)
- Log version + last reviewed date + approvers

Milestones (aligned to 6-week plan)
Week 1
- Inventory all existing FAQ/one-pagers/RFP answers and tag “keep / update / delete”
- Decide canonical Confluence locations + naming conventions
Week 2–3
- Draft v2 content + resolve open questions
Week 4
- Formal approval cycle; capture redlines; finalize safe evidence pointers
Week 5
- Publish Confluence canon + export PDFs; docs-site link hygiene (ENG-23310)
Week 6
- Rollout: Sales enablement notes; Slack announcement; HubSpot linking; maintenance plan

Notes to self (Naomi)
- Keep “Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private” differences as the repeating spine. Customers only believe what’s consistent across docs and what SEs say live.
- Every doc needs a “What we do NOT do” section to avoid misinterpretation (especially retention, logging, incident comms).
- Add a short “How to answer security questionnaires” blurb somewhere (maybe RFP library intro) + escalation triggers.

Immediate next actions
- [ ] Pull field feedback themes into a single list + map to sections (Markus Klein + Naomi)
- [ ] Confirm current retention defaults (Kevin) and update all mentions
- [ ] Confirm audit log event categories (Kevin + Marcus)
- [ ] Decide SCIM statement (Ethan + Kaitlyn + Naomi)
- [ ] Draft Confluence landing page stub with “single latest link” plan (Elliot + Isabelle)
